\section[orientar]{orientar — to guide, to orient; (orientar-se) to find your bearings}

\label{lesson:PT-C435-orientar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to regret, then the Portuguese for the compensation.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: orientar}
\textbf{orientar} — \textquotedblleft{}to guide, to orient; (orientar-se) to find your bearings\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Sem mapa, oriento-me pelo sol.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Without a map, I find my bearings by the sun.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Orientar-se} — to find your way. A teacher also \emph{orienta} a student's work.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{orientar} is built on \emph{oriente} 'east', which is inherited from Latin \emph{oriēns} 'rising', of the sun (EtymDB), from \emph{orīrī} 'to rise': first to face the east.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{orientar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{orientar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{orientar}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for to regret, then the Portuguese for the compensation, then say \emph{orientar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does orientar mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To guide, to orient; (orientar-se) to find your bearings\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[a bússola]{a bússola — the compass}

\label{lesson:PT-C435-bussola}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the compensation, then the Portuguese for to guide.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a bússola}
\textbf{a bússola} — \textquotedblleft{}the compass\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Na montanha, levamos sempre uma bússola.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{In the mountains, we always take a compass.}
\end{quote}

The needle points north.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{bússola} was borrowed from Italian \emph{bussola}, from Late Latin \emph{buxula} 'little box' (EtymDB), on \emph{buxus} 'boxwood': the needle sat in a small wooden box.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{a bússola}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{a bússola}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{a bússola}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for the compensation, then the Portuguese for to guide, then say \emph{a bússola} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does a bússola mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The compass\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[desorientado]{desorientado — lost, disoriented, confused}

\label{lesson:PT-C435-desorientado}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to guide, then the Portuguese for the compass.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: desorientado}
\textbf{desorientado} — \textquotedblleft{}lost, disoriented, confused\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Saí do metro completamente desorientado.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I came out of the metro completely disoriented.}
\end{quote}

Also confused about what to do: \emph{Estou desorientado com tantas opções}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{desorientado} is built from \emph{des-} 'un-' and \emph{orientado} 'oriented' (EtymDB), on \emph{orientar}, from Latin \emph{oriēns} 'rising (sun)'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{desorientado}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{desorientado}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{desorientado}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for to guide, then the Portuguese for the compass, then say \emph{desorientado} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does desorientado mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Lost, disoriented, confused\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[o roteiro]{o roteiro — the travel plan, the route guide}

\label{lesson:PT-C435-roteiro}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the compass, then the Portuguese for lost.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: o roteiro}
\textbf{o roteiro} — \textquotedblleft{}the travel plan, the route guide\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Fizemos um roteiro de três dias pela costa.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{We planned a three-day route along the coast.}
\end{quote}

In Brazil \emph{o roteiro} is also a film script.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{roteiro} is built on \emph{rota} 'route, course' with \emph{-eiro} (EtymDB); \emph{rota} is usually traced to Latin \emph{rupta (via)} 'broken (road)', from \emph{rumpere} 'to break' (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{o roteiro}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{o roteiro}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for the compass, then the Portuguese for lost, then say \emph{o roteiro} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[localizar]{localizar — to locate, to find}

\label{lesson:PT-C435-localizar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for lost, then the Portuguese for the travel plan.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: localizar}
\textbf{localizar} — \textquotedblleft{}to locate, to find\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Não consigo localizar o hotel no mapa.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I cannot find the hotel on the map.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Estar localizado} — to be located: \emph{A casa está bem localizada}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{localizar} is built on \emph{local} 'place', a learned borrowing from Late Latin \emph{locālis} (EtymDB), on \emph{locus} 'place'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{localizar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{localizar}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for lost, then the Portuguese for the travel plan, then say \emph{localizar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
